governance_label: Strategy + empowered regulator + binding institutional apparatus, longest-running in the region
source_name: Modulos Middle East AI Compliance Guide; digitalbricks.ai State of AI in the Middle East (2025)
rationale: UAE appointed the world's first Minister of State for AI in 2017, has a National AI Strategy (referenced today as the National AI Strategy 2031), and in May 2025 created a cabinet-level Regulatory Intelligence Office to use AI in drafting and updating federal law. Longest institutional track record of any country in the set.

governance_label: Strategy + dedicated authority + binding sectoral adoption framework
source_name: vision2030.ai Saudi National AI Strategy 2026 / SDAIA guide
rationale: SDAIA (established 2019) runs the National Strategy for Data and AI and released a binding AI Adoption Framework in May 2024; Saudi Arabia designated 2026 the 'Year of Artificial Intelligence.' Scored just below the UAE for a shorter institutional track record and no standalone AI law.

governance_label: Published national strategy; no independently confirmed dedicated AI regulator
source_name: Baker Institute working paper; ComputerWeekly -- Qatar launches Qai
rationale: Qatar published a national AI plan prior to 2022 and in Dec 2025 QIA launched Qai as a national AI infrastructure/commercialization champion -- but Qai reads as an investment and infrastructure vehicle rather than a regulatory authority; no dedicated independent AI regulator analogous to SDAIA was confirmed in this research pass.

governance_label: Published strategy; AI-specific law proposed and under development
source_name: The GCC Edge -- AI Governance in the Gulf: Budgets Shape the Rules
rationale: Search results indicate Bahrain has a national AI strategy and a proposed AI law in progress -- ahead of some GCC peers on the binding-regulation track even though the law is not yet enacted. Confidence is low pending a primary-source citation of the strategy document itself.

governance_label: Developing AI adoption framework tied to digital-transformation strategy
source_name: digitalbricks.ai -- State of AI in the Middle East (2025)
rationale: Kuwait has published a national AI strategy (per the Baker Institute's statement that all six GCC states have done so) and is developing an AI adoption framework linked to its digital-transformation plan, but no dedicated standalone AI authority was identified in this research pass.

governance_label: National AI Policy reported as still being finalized
source_name: digitalbricks.ai -- State of AI in the Middle East (2025)
rationale: Coverage describes Oman as 'finalizing' a National AI Policy as of this research pass, i.e. not yet published/final -- scored conservatively below states with a published strategy in force.

governance_label: Cabinet-approved national AI policy with dedicated implementation apparatus
source_name: Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad (ISSI) issue brief
rationale: Pakistan's federal cabinet unanimously approved the National AI Policy 2025 on 30 Jul 2025, establishing an AI Council, an implementation action matrix, and AI innovation/venture funds, with targets of 3 million AI-related jobs and 1 million trained AI professionals by 2030. Real institutional apparatus, though binding enforcement track record is not yet established.

governance_label: Updated national strategy + coordinating body + regulation-in-progress, no enacted AI law yet
source_name: SETAV -- Turkiye's 2026 AI Strategy and the Logic of Middle Power Autonomy; TRT World Research Centre -- Turkiye and the Future of AI Sovereignty
rationale: Turkey's 2026 AI strategy leverages TUBITAK BILGEM and defense-industrial player ASELSAN to address semiconductor/compute dependencies, with concrete targets (1GW of data-center capacity and 50,000 AI specialists by 2030). Regulatory development is active but not yet binding: Turkey is moving toward a risk-based, EU AI Act-inspired framework, and the TBMM (parliament) AI Research Commission is expected to release a report in late 2026 that may recommend sectoral AI laws. Scored above the 2025-session's prior 'Low confidence, unverified' entry now that a citable, dated 2026 source exists, but still below Bahrain/Saudi since no AI-specific law has been enacted and no dedicated standalone regulator (equivalent to SDAIA) exists yet -- TUBITAK is a research/coordination body, not a regulator.

governance_label: Dedicated cabinet-level regulatory apparatus + binding sectoral regulation already in force
source_name: Regulations.ai / White & Case AI Watch -- Israel; Lexology -- 'AI Use in the Financial Sector - Final Report of the Regulatory Workgroup' (Bank of Israel Directive 369)
rationale: Netanyahu appointed Israel's first AI Chief (Brig. Gen. res. Erez Askal) on 12 Oct 2025, heading a new National Artificial Intelligence Directorate in the PM's Office; the government approved broad AI policy on 16 Jun 2026 and the Directorate published a 5-year National AI Strategic Plan on 13 Aug 2026 (100,000+ accelerators, domestic quantum computer, sub-5nm fab target). Rather than one AI law, Israel runs a sector-based model (Dec 2023 'Responsible Innovation' policy) -- the clearest binding instance found is Bank of Israel Proper Conduct of Banking Business Directive 369 (updated 21 Aug 2024), which already covers AI/model-risk governance for banks; further binding Bank of Israel financial-sector AI directives are expected late 2025/early 2026 per a multi-regulator working group. Scored below UAE's 5 because the AI-specific institutional apparatus (Directorate) is only ~1 year old versus UAE's since-2017 track record.

governance_label: Presidentially-launched national strategy + standing cabinet-level coordinating council; binding AI law in the legislative pipeline, not yet enacted
source_name: OECD.AI -- Egypt National Artificial Intelligence Strategy; Digital Watch Observatory -- Egypt's national AI strategy, second edition 2025-2030
rationale: Egypt's National Council for Artificial Intelligence (NCAI) was established by Cabinet in Nov 2019, chaired by the Minister of Communications and IT; President Sisi announced the second-edition National AI Strategy (2025-2030) in Jan 2025 (six pillars, targets incl. 7.7% ICT GDP contribution and 30,000 AI experts by 2030), with an executive plan approved. AI-specific legislation -- expected to formalize a 'Center for Responsible AI' with audit/certification powers -- is reported moving through the parliamentary process in 2025-2026 but was not confirmed enacted in this research pass. Matches this project's Tier-3 precedent (cabinet-approved strategy + coordinating body, binding regulation in progress but not yet law).

governance_label: Cabinet-approved national AI strategy + dedicated coordinating ministry unit; no binding AI-specific law or standalone regulator yet
source_name: Jordan News -- 'Cabinet approves Jordan's AI strategy for 2023-2027' (Cabinet Decision No. 659)
rationale: Jordan's Council of Ministers formally approved the National AI Strategy and Implementation Roadmap (2023-2027) via Cabinet Decision No. 659 dated 20 Dec 2022 -- a five-year plan with 68 projects across five pillars (incl. a legislative/regulatory pillar) and a dedicated AI division inside the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship (established 2020). Jordan has also adopted a National Charter of Ethics for AI. No binding, enacted AI-specific law or independent AI regulator (akin to SDAIA) was found -- matching this project's Tier-3 precedent, same tier as Pakistan's row.

governance_label: Strategy launched + PM-chaired coordinating committee, but strategy still described as being refined 18+ months after launch; no independent AI regulator
source_name: Iraq Business News -- First Meeting of Iraq Supreme Committee for AI (Aug 2024); Iraq Business News -- AI Strategy Meeting at Iraq's Ministry of Planning (Apr 2026)
rationale: Iraq's Higher/Supreme Committee for Artificial Intelligence, chaired by Prime Minister Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani, formally launched the Iraqi National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (INSAIN) 2024-2030 in late 2024. However, an April 2026 Ministry of Planning meeting was still 'refining the strategy's goals to meet Ministry of Planning standards,' and a separate proposal to create a dedicated AI Ministry/independent authority remains unactioned -- suggesting the strategy, while launched at cabinet/PM level, is not yet a finalized, binding instrument and no dedicated standalone regulator exists. Scored 3 rather than 4; Low confidence reflects genuine ambiguity about whether INSAIN counts as 'published' or still in draft after 18+ months.

governance_label: Dedicated cabinet-level AI ministry (MITAI) + published 2025-2030 national strategy, but no binding AI-specific law yet
source_name: TahawulTech.com -- Lebanon joins global tech race with appointment of its first Ministry of AI; Levellers.ai -- AI Regulation in Lebanon
rationale: Lebanon created the Ministry of State for Technology and Artificial Intelligence (MITAI) in early 2025 under Minister Kamal Shehadi -- a dedicated cabinet-level ministry, institutionally stronger than most GCC peers' coordinating committees. On 7 November 2025 MITAI launched the National Digital Transformation and AI Strategy 2025-2030, targeting growth of AI/digital's GDP contribution from $1.3bn (2025) to $3.5bn by 2030. However, AI is currently governed only indirectly (via Law 81/2018 on electronic transactions/data and sector rules) -- no AI-specific binding law or independent regulator distinct from the policy-making ministry was found, so this falls short of level 4.

governance_label: No known published or drafted national AI strategy identified; AI appears only as a conference theme and sector-specific cooperation MoUs
source_name: SANA -- Syria highlights AI role in modernizing government services at Dubai forum; Licentium -- Syria AI regulation overview
rationale: Syria's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology hosted a first regional AI conference in Damascus in 2025 and has signed cooperation agreements (e.g. with the Arab ICT Organization, and on AI-assisted efforts against hate speech in media, July 2025), reflecting genuine early institutional attention to AI under the new government. However, no source found identifies a published or even drafted national AI strategy document -- one specialist regulatory tracker explicitly states Syria has 'no general AI licence, no high-risk AI classification law, no general AI transparency statute.' Scored 0 rather than 1 because there is not yet a named strategy-in-progress to point to, only conference/MoU-level activity; this is inherently a hard absence to prove and should be treated as provisional (Low confidence) pending a dedicated follow-up search once Syria's new government's institutions mature further.

governance_label: Cabinet/Supreme-Council-approved strategy + coordinating body + a binding sectoral law already enforced, but the regulator itself was shelved and revived within the same year
source_name: Filterwatch -- Control Over Innovation: Iran's Paradoxical AI Development, Part 1 (Sept 2025); Mehr News -- Iran to launch national artificial intelligence organization
rationale: Iran's Supreme Council of the Cultural Revolution approved a National Artificial Intelligence Document in June 2024, and a National Artificial Intelligence Organization (NAIO) was established under presidential supervision in July 2024. Iran's 2025 Law on Combating the Spread of Untrue News Content is a binding, enforced framework (digital-watermarking and 'High-Impact' AI model registration requirements, enforcement via FATA cyber police) -- a real sectoral law already in force, which would argue for a 4. However, the NAIO itself was reportedly shelved in May 2025 and revived only four days later by a Majlis-approved AI Bill, with formal re-establishment not finalized until an October 2025 Majlis vote -- institutional instability that falls short of the UAE/Saudi pattern of a single, sustained empowered regulator. Scored 3 to reflect real binding regulation plus a coordinating body whose institutional footing is still unsettled.

governance_label: No known national AI strategy -- conflict and split administration have stalled digital-policy development entirely
source_name: Levellers.ai -- AI Regulation in Yemen: Law, Status and Gaps
rationale: Unlike most MENA states, Yemen has no published or officially adopted national AI strategy, roadmap, or AI-specific law as of this research pass. Yemen's Ministry of Telecommunications and IT exists in duplicate (an Aden-government version and a Sana'a/Houthi-authority version), and both are focused on repairing war-damaged infrastructure rather than AI policymaking. Yemen is nominally covered by the pan-Arab Digital Agenda 2023-2033 but has not produced its own strategy. Confidence marked Medium rather than High because this rests on a single secondary aggregator source rather than a government primary source (none appears to exist to check against).

governance_label: No known national AI strategy -- Taliban authorities have restricted rather than advanced digital infrastructure
rationale: As of May 2026, Afghanistan has no comprehensive AI law, sectoral AI rules, voluntary AI principles, or national AI strategy; the legal framework since August 2021 is grounded entirely in the Taliban's interpretation of Sharia law with no AI-specific instrument enacted or formally proposed. If anything the Taliban government has moved in the opposite direction, imposing deliberate internet blackouts in late 2025 (severing fiber-optic lines and shutting down telecommunications) rather than building AI governance capacity.
